product.title: the five-year pictures, the zone counts, the recent radar hail cells and the bubble anchors

standing.claim: A malformed radar value or a bad join reference aborts the whole history build, so no part is written. D16 says each part fails alone.
standing.evidence: build() catches only HistoryError, OSError, ValueError and KeyError (except clauses at lines 756, 806, 843, 861). A null tenths value in one radar cell raises TypeError at line 327 (scan_radar); a join reference of 99999 raises IndexError at line 546 (count_zones). Both runs exit 1 with a traceback and write nothing. Throwaway store copies F1 and F2, run under /home/user/hail-b5/out/b6/review/P4 (scratch since removed).
standing.fix: Catch Exception per part, or add TypeError and IndexError to each except, and validate row shapes in scan_radar, scan_climate and count_zones so bad rows raise HistoryError. Add tests where a null tenths value and an out-of-range join reference each leave the other parts built.

standing.claim: The labels unavailable command fails open. One unreadable shard stops it, and the labels block still reads loaded, so stale bubbles stay drawable (D20).
standing.evidence: unavailable() reads every shard without a guard (lines 471-473). In test F3 a truncated shard stopped it after 4 of 28 shards: 24 shards still carried flags, and hail/index.json still said labels state loaded. main() catches only LabelError and HistoryError (line 682), so the traceback exits 1 and the block is never rewritten.
standing.fix: Guard each shard, count the failures, write the unavailable block before the loop, and return 0 with the failures named. Add a test with one corrupt shard that asserts every readable shard is cleared and the block reads unavailable.

standing.claim: A joins index with no zone lists aborts the whole history build before any part is written. The zone list is read outside the zones failure handler, so the pictures and the recent list are lost although they need no zones.
standing.evidence: codes = _zone_public_codes(index) runs before the zones try (which starts at line 818). It raises at line 483 when the lists are empty, so build exits 1 with no files written (test F6b: joins zone lists emptied and joins marked unavailable). The pictures are computed earlier (lines 748-811) and then discarded.
standing.fix: Move the code list inside the zones try, so an empty list is a zones failure only.

standing.claim: Shards that fail in labels build keep their old flags, and a missing or unreadable font leaves the old flags in place under a non-loaded block. D20 says no stale bubble can be drawn.
standing.evidence: A shard whose outline has no point raises KeyError and is skipped with continue (lines 433-435). The file keeps 895 flagged outlines and the block reads partial (test F4). When the font check fails, build() returns at lines 405-412 before touching any shard, and 895 flagged outlines remain under an unavailable block (test F5). The docstring (lines 40-44) names the unavailable command as the remedy, but build() never calls it. _font() (line 110) also lets an OSError from ImageFont.truetype escape, so an unreadable font file crashes the build instead of marking it unavailable.
standing.fix: For each failed shard, rewrite it without k and kv when it parses, and make the browser draw no bubble unless the labels block is loaded. Catch OSError in _font() and raise LabelError.

standing.claim: A bad zone outline download is cached before it is checked, and the cached copy is reused on every later run until someone deletes the cache file.
standing.evidence: get_zone_file writes the response body to the cache at line 709 before anything checks it. read_zone_outlines checks it later (line 855). With an HTML body in the cache (test F6) the outlines are unavailable on the first and the second run, and the bad file was still there, unchanged, after the second run.
standing.fix: Validate the body first (parse it and run read_zone_outlines on a temporary file), and write the cache only when it is valid. When a cached file fails to parse, delete it and fetch once more.

standing.claim: Bubbles are placed above the dot only, so coverage falls short of the stage-1 measured rule that the docstring cites as its source.
standing.evidence: final.py tries the above box and then the below box for each cluster (lines 42-56). The module's place() (lines 216-235) tries only box_for, which is above. On the two test tiles, zoom 17 covers 10,234 of 11,192 outlines above-only (91.4 percent) against 11,028 with below allowed (98.5 percent, 487 below placements). Zoom 18 covers 10,925 (97.6 percent) against 11,187 (99.96 percent). Statewide the module covers 95.25 percent at zoom 17 and 98.78 percent at zoom 18 (labels-statewide.json). The owner's reference asks for a value bubble on every house (research/map-b6/README.md lines 15 and 102). The docstring at line 14 calls the rule the measured Rule B, which it is not in this respect.
standing.fix: Owner decision. Either encode the side in k (0 none, 1 above, 2 below), a format change the integrator must approve, or keep above-only and state the coverage loss in the report and the docstring, and drop the claim that the rule is the measured Rule B.

standing.claim: After the labels pass, 36 building shards exceed the 250,000-byte split limit, so the buildings verify check would fail on the labelled store.
standing.evidence: I measured every shard of the adopted store with the labels rule: 0 shards over 250,000 bytes before, 36 after. The largest is r0068_c01801.json at 262,318 bytes. SHARD_BYTES is at line 79, the split test at line 962, and the verify rejection at lines 1662-1663. The daily order runs verify before the labels step, so it passes today. r0061_c0150 is 257,720 bytes raw and 45,053 bytes gzip-9, which matches the builder's figure.
standing.fix: Integrator and owner decision before merge: count the flag bytes in the split rule (a buildings.py change), raise the limit (D26), or shorten the flags. Record the choice in the report.

standing.claim: The five-year pictures and the recent list skip the 95 percent season coverage rule that the summary applies to the same radar_1in row, and the legend does not say that the store is missing a radar day.
standing.evidence: summary.py tests coverage before it counts (line 1564, D37). history_layers counts days per cell with no coverage test (lines 328-332). The store index lists one missing day (missing_days ['2022-06-08'], days_present 1825 of 1826), so a cell can be under-counted by at most one day. The legend (lines 155-157) does not mention it.
standing.fix: Show the missing days in the sidecar and the legend (the index already holds them), or apply the season coverage rule before counting and show Data unavailable for a short season.

standing.claim: The docstring and the source terms quote the IEM permission with words it does not contain.
standing.evidence: Lines 27 and 686 quote free to use for any lawful purpose. joins.py line 532 quotes free to use these services for any lawful purpose. The as-is wording matches joins.py line 531.
standing.fix: Quote the words exactly, or use an ellipsis.

standing.claim: The docstring says a bad picture keeps the recent list, but a radar read failure removes both hail1 and recent together.
standing.evidence: The code (lines 758-764) marks both unavailable, which is the correct conservative behaviour because a missing shard cannot be counted. The docstring at lines 43-44 says otherwise.
standing.fix: Correct the docstring to say that a radar read failure takes the picture and the recent list together.

standing.claim: RadarScan.top is computed for the whole state (a 49 MB int16 array) and read only by a test.
standing.evidence: Lines 282, 298 and 338. The product never reads it. tests/test_history_layers.py reads it.
standing.fix: Compute it in the test helper, or drop it from the product.

standing.claim: The labels docstrings cite an absolute path outside the repository, a brief, and two modules that are not in the repository.
standing.evidence: Line 14 gives /home/user/hail-b5/out/b6/design/bubbles/final.py. Line 18 says the brief writes 56 px. Lines 116, 145, 154 and 162 cite place.py and extract.py, which are not in this repository.
standing.fix: Name the rule and its place in the repository, and remove the out-of-repository path and the brief reference.

standing.claim: The has-a-value test is tenths > 0 instead of the 64-tenth floor the docstring states and the brief sets.
standing.evidence: Lines 132, 139 and 253; docstring line 11. No effect today: across all 4,597 radar shards of the adopted store there are 2,638,537 positive values and the smallest is 64.
standing.fix: Use hail.FLOOR_TENTHS (hail.py line 68) as the test.

standing.claim: Cells that had radar data but no stored estimate of 0.25 in or more show Data unavailable (drawn as a dash). The wording reads as missing data.
standing.evidence: Lines 130-141; the legend is at history_layers.py lines 168-169. The count is 29,483 of 483,008 zoom-17 bubbles statewide. The brief specifies this word, so this is a wording decision for the owner. No estimate of 0.25 in or more says what the store knows.

standing.claim: The zone legend does not say that a zero is a count of archived products, not an all-clear. The sheet's summary says so.
standing.fix: Add the sentence to the zone legend.

pending.claim: A --tiles run writes a block marked loaded that covers only the named tiles.
pending.fix: Mark the block partial for a subset run, or keep the full-store block.

pending.claim: The overall state counts failure entries rather than parts, so a partial zones part plus three failed parts reads unavailable.
pending.evidence: Line 867. A radar failure adds two entries, so the count does not match the parts.

pending.claim: The store index is written before the picture, zone and manifest files, so a crash between the steps leaves blocks that name files not on disk.
pending.fix: Write the files, then the manifest, then the index.

pending.claim: The sidecar gives bytes and SHA-256 only for the two pictures. The brief says the sidecar gives these for each file.
pending.evidence: Lines 869-874. The zones and recent files sit in the index blocks instead.
pending.fix: Add them to the sidecar, or amend the brief.

pending.claim: verify compares the recent list by cell key only, not by each cell's day list.
Outside P4's files: a stage-1 research file on this branch names two commercial vendors many times, which the repository's vendor-name rule would flag.
pending.fix: The supervisor decides whether research notes are exempt from the rule.

pending.claim: The totals_over_103_zones figures are sums of per-zone counts, so a polygon that touches three zones counts three times. They are not Montana totals.
pending.evidence: The sums match my independent recount (for example high_wind_warnings 2544 and flood_advisories 1713), so the numbers are right; only the label is misleading.
pending.fix: Label them as sums over zones, or do not quote them as Montana totals.
